extracted.intended_audience: chemical manufacturers, importers, distributors, employers, and OSHA compliance officers
extracted.subtask_short: OSHA HCS labeling and SDS compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for classifying hazardous chemicals and for preparing, labeling, distributing, updating, and making available Safety Data Sheets (SDSs) and container labels under OSHA's Hazard Communication Standard (29 CFR 1910.1200).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and scope of §1910.1200
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of this section is to ensure that the hazards of all chemicals produced or imported are classified, and that information concerning the classified hazards is transmitted to employers and employees. The requirements of this section are intended to be consistent with the provisions of the United Nations Globally Harmonized System of Classification and Labeling of Chemicals (GHS), primarily Revision 7. The transmittal of information is to be accomplished by means of comprehensive hazard communication programs, which are to include container labeling and other forms of warning, safety data sheets and employee training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the regulatory objective (classification + transmission) and the required mechanisms (labels, SDSs, training). Indicates alignment with UN GHS Revision 7 as the basis for criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification obligations for chemical manufacturers and importers
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical manufacturers and importers shall evaluate chemicals produced in their workplaces or imported by them to classify the chemicals in accordance with this section. For each chemical, the chemical manufacturer or importer shall determine the hazard classes, and where appropriate, the category of each class that apply to the chemical being classified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification must include hazards associated with the chemical's intrinsic properties including (A) a change in the chemical's physical form and (B) chemical reaction products associated with known or reasonably anticipated uses or applications. Employers are not required to classify chemicals if they choose to rely on the classification performed by the chemical manufacturer or importer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling requirements for shipped containers (label elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: The chemical manufacturer, importer, or distributor shall ensure that each container of hazardous chemicals leaving the workplace is labeled, tagged or marked. Where the chemical manufacturer, importer, or distributor is required to label, tag or mark the following shall be provided: (i) Product identifier; (ii) Signal word; (iii) Hazard statement(s); (iv) Pictogram(s); (v) Precautionary statement(s); (vi) Name, U.S. address, and U.S. telephone number of the chemical manufacturer, importer, or other responsible party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hazards not otherwise classified and hazards identified and classified under (d)(1)(ii) do not have to be addressed on the container. 'Label elements' are the specified pictogram, hazard statement, signal word and precautionary statement for each hazard class and category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation labeling and compatibility with DOT requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical manufacturers, importers, or distributors shall ensure that each container of hazardous chemicals leaving the workplace is labeled, tagged, or marked in accordance with this section in a manner which does not conflict with the requirements of the Hazardous Materials Transportation Act and regulations issued by the Department of Transportation (49 CFR subtitle B). The label for bulk shipments of hazardous chemicals must be on the immediate container, transmitted with the shipping papers or the bills of lading, or, with the agreement of the receiving entity, transmitted by technological or electronic means so that it is immediately available to workers in printed form on the receiving end of shipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a DOT-required pictogram appears on a shipped container, the pictogram specified in appendix C.4 to this section for the same hazard is not required on the label.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label update timing and obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical manufacturers, importers, distributors, or employers who become newly aware of any significant information regarding the hazards of a chemical shall revise the labels for the chemical within six months of becoming aware of the new information, and shall ensure that labels on containers of hazardous chemicals shipped after that time contain the new information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For chemicals already released for shipment and awaiting distribution, entities may elect not to relabel those containers; however, if not relabeled they must either provide the updated label with each shipment or, with agreement of the receiving entity, transmit the labels by electronic or other technological means. If the chemical is not currently produced or imported, the information must be added to the label before the chemical is shipped or introduced into the workplace again.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small container labeling exceptions and outer package requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the chemical manufacturer, importer, or distributor can demonstrate that it is not feasible to use pull-out labels, fold-back labels, or tags containing the full label information: (ii) For a container ≤100 ml, the label must include at minimum: (A) Product identifier; (B) Pictogram(s); (C) Signal word; (D) Chemical manufacturer's name and phone number; and (E) A statement that the full label information for the hazardous chemical is provided on the immediate outer package. (iii) For a container ≤3 ml where any label interferes with normal use, no label is required, but the container must bear, at minimum, the product identifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For all small containers covered by these provisions, the immediate outer package must include the full label information required by paragraph (f)(1) for each hazardous chemical in the immediate outer package, the label must not be removed or defaced, and the small containers must be stored in the immediate outer package bearing the complete label when not in use.

rubrics_metrics.name: SDS creation and workplace maintenance obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical manufacturers and importers shall obtain or develop a safety data sheet for each hazardous chemical they produce or import. Employers shall have a safety data sheet in the workplace for each hazardous chemical which they use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SDSs are a core means of transmitting hazard information from manufacturers/importers to employers and employees; employers must maintain SDSs for chemicals in their workplace.

rubrics_metrics.name: SDS content, language, and section ordering requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The chemical manufacturer or importer shall ensure that the safety data sheet is in English (although the employer may maintain copies in other languages as well), and includes at least the following section numbers and headings, and associated information under each heading, in the order listed: (i) Section 1, Identification; (ii) Section 2, Hazard(s) identification; (iii) Section 3, Composition/information on ingredients; (iv) Section 4, First-aid measures; (v) Section 5, Fire-fighting measures; (vi) Section 6, Accidental release measures; (vii) Section 7, Handling and storage; (viii) Section 8, Exposure controls/personal protection; (ix) Section 9, Physical and chemical properties; (x) Section 10, Stability and reactivity; (xi) Section 11, Toxicological information; (xii) Section 12, Ecological information; (xiii) Section 13, Disposal considerations; (xiv) Section 14, Transport information; (xv) Section 15, Regulatory information; and (xvi) Section 16, Other information, including date of preparation or last revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: To be consistent with the GHS, an SDS must also include headings in paragraphs (g)(2)(xii) through (g)(2)(xv). OSHA will not be enforcing information requirements in sections 12 through 15, as these areas are not under its jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distributor obligations for providing SDSs and updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Distributors shall ensure that safety data sheets, and updated information, are provided to other distributors and employers with their initial shipment and with the first shipment after a safety data sheet is updated; the distributor shall either provide SDSs with the shipped containers, or send them to the other distributor or employer prior to or at the time of the shipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retail distributors selling hazardous chemicals to employers having a commercial account shall provide an SDS to such employers upon request and shall post a sign or otherwise inform them that an SDS is available. Wholesale distributors shall also provide SDSs upon request. Chemical manufacturers, importers, and distributors need not provide SDSs to retail distributors that have informed them that the retail distributor does not sell the product to commercial accounts or open the sealed container to use it in their own workplaces. If an employer without a commercial account purchases from a retail distributor not required to have SDS on file, the retail distributor must provide the manufacturer/importer/distributor contact information upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workplace SDS accessibility and storage format
rubrics_metrics.description: Safety data sheets may be kept in any form, including as operating procedures, and may be stored in such a way to cover groups of hazardous chemicals in a work area where it may be more appropriate to address the hazards of a process rather than individual hazardous chemicals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, the employer shall ensure that in all cases the required information is provided for each hazardous chemical, and is readily accessible during each work shift to employees when they are in their work area(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade secret claim requirements for SDSs (with concentration ranges)
rubrics_metrics.description: The chemical manufacturer, importer, or employer may withhold the specific chemical identity, including the chemical name, other specific identification of a hazardous chemical, and/or the exact percentage (concentration) or concentration range of the substance in a mixture, from section 3 of the safety data sheet, provided that: (i) The claim that the information withheld is a trade secret can be supported; (ii) Information contained in the safety data sheet concerning the properties and effects of the hazardous chemical is disclosed; (iii) The safety data sheet indicates that the specific chemical identity and/or concentration or concentration range of composition is being withheld as a trade secret; (iv) If the concentration or concentration range is being claimed as a trade secret then the safety data sheet provides the ingredient's concentration as one of the prescribed ranges below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribed concentration ranges (must use narrowest possible): (A) 0.1% to 1%; (B) 0.5% to 1.5%; (C) 1% to 5%; (D) 3% to 7%; (E) 5% to 10%; (F) 7% to 13%; (G) 10% to 30%; (H) 15% to 40%; (I) 30% to 60%; (J) 45% to 70%; (K) 60% to 80%; (L) 65% to 85%; (M) 80% to 100%.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and applicability of 'Article'
rubrics_metrics.description: Article means a manufactured item other than a fluid or particle: (i) Which is formed to a specific shape or design during manufacture; (ii) Which has end use function(s) dependent in whole or in part upon its shape or design during end use; and (iii) Which under normal conditions of use does not release more than very small quantities, e.g., minute or trace amounts of a hazardous chemical (as determined under paragraph (d) of this section), and does not pose a physical hazard or health risk to employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition determines whether an item is covered as a 'chemical' under the HCS or treated as an 'article' exempt from some requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label elements and signal words/pictograms definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Label elements means the specified pictogram, hazard statement, signal word and precautionary statement for each hazard class and category. Signal word means a word used to indicate the relative level of severity of hazard and alert the reader to a potential hazard on the label; the signal words used in this section are 'danger' and 'warning.' 'Danger' is used for the more severe hazards, while 'warning' is used for the less severe. Pictogram means a composition that may include a symbol plus other graphic elements, such as a border, background pattern, or color, that is intended to convey specific information about the hazards of a chemical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eight pictograms are designated under this standard for application to a hazard category. Hazard statement means a statement assigned to a hazard class and category that describes the nature of the hazard(s) of a chemical, including, where appropriate, the degree of hazard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of key terms relevant to classification and compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms defined include: chemical; chemical name; chemical manufacturer; hazard category; hazardous chemical; hazard class; hazard not otherwise classified (HNOC); health hazard; physical hazard; combustible dust; container; product identifier; safety data sheet (SDS); precautionary statement; specific chemical identity; trade secret; use; workplace; work area; and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many definitions cross-reference appendices (e.g., Appendix A for Health Hazard Criteria, Appendix B for Physical Hazard Criteria) which contain the specific criteria for determining classification of health and physical hazards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by Reference (IBR) materials: applicability and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain material is incorporated by reference into this part with the approval of the Director of the Federal Register in accordance with 5 U.S.C. 552(a) and 1 CFR part 51. To enforce any edition other than that specified in this section, OSHA must publish a document in the Federal Register and the material must be available to the public. Only the mandatory provisions (i.e., provisions containing the word 'shall' or other mandatory language) of standards incorporated by reference are adopted as standards under the Occupational Safety and Health Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All approved IBR material is available for inspection at OSHA and at the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA). Contact information and a list of sources (ANSI, ASTM, ISO, IEC, UN publications, etc.) are provided for obtaining IBR materials. Changes to IBR materials and historic files are available for inspection in the OSHA Docket Office.
